decision.governing_rule: rule 4: external recognition required for L7+, cannot be inferred from internal reputation alone
decision.alternative_reasoning:
Scope of impact, autonomy, ownership, and influence evidence read on their face as L7 (company-wide impact, authority spanning the full roadmap, sign-off gating every team). L7 was not assigned because rule 4 makes external recognition a hard gate for L7+, and the JD explicitly states no publications, patents, or external presentations -- the reputation is internal only. Per rule 4 this cannot be inferred or waived, so L7 is unavailable regardless of how strong the internal-scope case is.</alternative_reasoning>

decision.reasoning:
All six factors point clearly to L6 or above: scope is company-wide across an entire multi-generation roadmap (NX-400 through NX-600), autonomy is final sign-off authority without further review, problem complexity involves cross-core strategic PPA tradeoffs, ownership scope (5a) is architecture direction for a product line across generations, and influence spans every core team company-wide. This would ordinarily push toward L7 given the breadth of company-wide authority described. However, rule 4 is explicit and non-negotiable: L7 and above require external recognition (publications, patents, standards bodies, external reputation), and this cannot be inferred from internal reputation alone. The job description explicitly states the incumbent has never published, patented, or presented outside the company and that the reputation is entirely internal. This caps the role at L6 regardless of the strength of the internal scope/influence evidence. Note: the eight-years-in-role detail is experience/tenure and was explicitly excluded from the rating rationale per the experience-is-not-a-factor rule.

Source organization calibration: source is a 104-person late-stage private company (small, under ~150 headcount), which per section 6 carries an expected drift of titles mapping DOWN 1-2 levels due to title inflation and shallow org depth (org_depth=4 here, consistent with a flatter small-org structure). The assigned L6 is one level below the internally-implied L7 scope, which is directionally consistent with that small-company drift prior -- the external-recognition gate happens to align with what the size-based prior would also predict, which raises confidence somewhat. Platform dependency is low, so no cap was applied to technical depth/breadth. Overall this result is consistent with the section 6 prior rather than contradicting it.</reasoning>
